drafted_from: tool:check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference's row in tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/tool-rows.json, do-work/check-motion.mjs, read-data/motion-bar.mjs, read-data/measure-motion.mjs and test/check-motion.test.mjs; the answers were observed by running the command on ffmpeg test clips
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check that clips/draft.mp4 moves as much as clips/reference.mp4, which I am copying; its end card starts at 5 seconds, and my bar is in bar.json." It measures both videos on your computer and tells you whether the draft passed each row of your bar.
no_lists_because: It names no list: the bar is a JSON file of kind motion-bar that your AI writes from your own records, and the videos are files on your computer.
instructions: 1. On your computer, clone the Workshop checkout and run brew install ffmpeg (this brings ffprobe). Run everything from the root of the checkout.

2. Write your bar to a file, for example bar.json: {"kind":"motion-bar","rows":[{"name":"moving","bar_key":"moving_min","measure":"moving_share","relation":"at_least","times_reference":0.5},{"name":"hold","bar_key":"hold_max_s","measure":"longest_hold_s","relation":"at_most","times_reference":3}]}. Each row names a measure (moving_share, longest_hold_s or holds_over_1s_per_min), a relation (at_least or at_most) and either times_reference (a multiple of the reference's own value) or value (a fixed number).

3. Say to your AI: "Check my draft's motion against the reference." It reads the row with tools:list {tool}, then runs: node tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/do-work/check-motion.mjs --reference clips/reference.mp4 --render clips/draft.mp4 --end-card-start 5 --bar bar.json

4. Read the last line: {"result": {still_threshold, reference, draft, bar, pass, verdict}}. verdict is passed only when every row in pass is true; a failed verdict still exits 0. An {"error": ...} line says what to change (a missing flag or file, an end card second of 0 or less, a bar that is not a motion-bar, a measure name the tool does not give).

worked_examples.title: A moving clip passes against itself; the same bar fails a still grey clip
worked_examples.ask: Check that clips/flat.mp4 moves as much as clips/reference.mp4, end card at 5 seconds.
worked_examples.given: Run locally from the Workshop checkout after tools:list: node tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/do-work/check-motion.mjs --reference clips/reference.mp4 --render clips/flat.mp4 --end-card-start 5 --bar bar.json. clips/reference.mp4 is a 6 second 160x120 15 fps ffmpeg testsrc2 pattern, clips/flat.mp4 is 6 seconds of plain grey, and bar.json is the two-row bar of step 2 (the clips and bar are made as in tools/check-a-videos-motion-against-a-reference/test/check-motion.test.mjs). Read from do-work/check-motion.mjs and observed by running it; with --render clips/reference.mp4 the same bar gives verdict passed.
